messages:
Ash: starting a combined PRD/RFC thread for Private deployments (VPC + on-prem). goal: finalize connectivity options, acceptance tests, and edge-case list. tagging Sarah, Mike, Eva, Leigh for reviews.

Sarah: quick preference note — split acceptance criteria per deployment mode in the doc (VPC vs on-prem). single RFC is fine as long as sections are clear.

Mike: listing practical connectivity modes for MVP: 1) customer NAT with stable egress IPs, 2) outbound mTLS tunnel/proxy, 3) fully offline on-prem bundle. major risks: asymmetric routing, MTU/fragmentation on long gRPC streams, split-horizon DNS, and BGP instability if we support peering.

Eva: security requirements to include: external KMS/CMK support (HSM optional), audit log forwarding with retention knobs, strict data residency language (no unencrypted escapes), and cert rotation policy for mTLS (<=30 days plus emergency rotation instructions).

Leigh: ops items: ip rotation policy (DNS-first, IPs may change; announce 7-day deprecation), circuit-breaker behavior if continuous failures exceed threshold (failover or degrade SLO), and NAT port exhaustion runbook.

Ash: draft acceptance criteria (MVP v stretch):
MVP:
- mTLS tunnel: mutual auth, automated cert renewal, setup guide + healthcheck endpoints
- NAT-static-egress: customers supply static egress IP(s) or accept published FQDNs; Redwood publishes required ports/hosts
- On-prem offline: signed runtime artifacts and an installer with documented offline update path
Stretch:
- BGP peering with filtering, IPv6-native support, fine-grained per-tenant egress controls

Mike: add MTU requirement: default minimum MTU 1400 for gRPC/streaming; include an automated MTU verification test in CI. Also include a test for port exhaustion scenarios.

Ash: adding a sample firewall snippet for customer handoff. please copy into runbook where appropriate:
```
# customer firewall example
# allow outbound control plane and telemetry
ALLOW tcp 443 to control.private.redwood.example.net
ALLOW tcp 8443 to proxy.private.redwood.example.net
ALLOW udp 123 to ntp.private.redwood.example.net
```

Leigh: ops nit — we can't promise immutable CIDRs forever. provide a subscription feed (webhook/DNS changefeed) and a 7-day deprecation window for any IP changes. include escalation contact in the feed.

Eva: edge cases to call out explicitly: IPv6-only customers (MVP requires dual-stack or NAT64), DNS poisoning/split-horizon (recommend mTLS + pinned certs), and intermittent NAT port exhaustion. Also require retention override consent for any traces Redwood retains for diagnostics.

Sarah: customer asks prioritized: Customer-Delta and Customer-Fjord want mTLS tunnel first. mark mTLS as MVP priority; static-egress whitelisting as secondary.

Ash: timeline proposal: draft posted Wed 2025-03-12, reviews close Fri 2025-03-14, eng signoff Mon 2025-03-17, internal beta in ~3 sprints. reviewers: Mike/Eva/Leigh by Thu/Fri.

Ash: sample acceptance test to include in testkit:
```
# verify control plane reachability via static egress
curl -v --resolve api.private.redwood:443:52.11.101.45 https://api.private.redwood/health
# expect 200 and {"status":"ok"}
```

Mike: network-level test for fragmentation and throughput:
```
# run large gRPC payload test to surface MTU/fragmentation issues
python tests/grpc_mtu_test.py --host api.private.redwood --size 256000
```

Ash: billing note — distinguish proxied mTLS traffic from direct egress for metering and show egress costs in billing dashboard.

Leigh: handoff checklist (to include in PRD): netops contact + escalation, expected ip/fqdn list + subscription link, signed AUP/ICLA, scheduled maintenance window for cutover.

InfraBot: deploy template created: https://redwood/internals/deploy-templates/private-networking (auto-posted).

Sarah: action items: Ash to finalize PRD with clear VPC vs on-prem sections (due Wed 2025-03-12). Mike: detailed network acceptance tests + MTU tests (due Thu). Eva: security/compliance language (due Thu). Leigh: runbooks + ops playbook (due Fri). Everyone: leave inline comments by Fri.

Ash: any other missing edge cases? i'm worried about very short-lived NAT mappings (carrier networks) and mobile egress causing frequent reconnects.

Mike: add recommendation: enable TCP keepalive and reduce reconnect backoff for flaky egress, and offer connection pooling/proxying guidance.

Eva: add retention override controls and explicit opt-in for any diagnostic artifacts retained by Redwood.

Ash: thanks — i'll push a PR and tag reviewers when it's up. :rocket:
